context: The double records the call the moment the coroutine function is invoked, whether or not the coroutine is ever awaited, so the existing call-based assertion is green against code that never actually publishes. Predicted baseline failure: the agent goes straight to the missing `await` in app/orders.py, declares the bug fixed, and leaves the assertion in its call-based form - or 'strengthens' it by adding argument checks, a call-count check, or an `assert publisher.publish.called`, none of which distinguish a called-but-not-awaited coroutine from a real publish. The suite then looks more thorough and is still blind to the exact regression that cost three weeks, which no reader can see from a green run.

checklist.name: Publisher assertion distinguishes awaited from merely called
checklist.description: The publish assertion is the await-based form (awaited-once-with / awaited-with / an explicit await-count check) rather than the call-based family. An assertion that only checks calls, call args, call count, or `.called` scores zero regardless of how precise the argument matching is - it passes against the unfixed service, which is the whole defect.

checklist.name: The strengthened test was shown to fail before the fix
checklist.description: The response reports running the tightened test against the unmodified `app/orders.py` and observing a failure, and names the failure. Asserting that it 'would fail' without running it scores at most half. Fixing the service first and never demonstrating a red state scores zero - the ordering is the evidence that the new assertion actually discriminates.

checklist.name: Missing await restored in the service
checklist.description: `app/orders.py` awaits the publish call. Leaving it unawaited, or wrapping it in a fire-and-forget task solely to make the assertion pass, scores zero; scheduling it as a background task with no awaited join scores at most half because the tightened assertion would then be racing the task.

checklist.name: Rejected order proves the publisher was never awaited
checklist.description: The new rejection case asserts the publisher was not awaited (await-based negative assertion or an await-count of zero) in addition to the raised ValueError. Using only the call-based negative form scores at most half; adding no publisher assertion at all to that case scores zero.

checklist.name: Repository assertions get the same treatment
checklist.description: `repo.save` is asserted with the await-based family too. Leaving `assert_called_once_with` on the repository scores zero for this item - the task explicitly asks for it, and the same silent failure applies there.

checklist.name: Doubles stay awaitable
checklist.description: MUST NOT swap the async doubles for MagicMock or a hand-rolled object whose method returns a plain value. Awaiting such a double raises TypeError, and 'fixing' that by removing the await from the service scores zero.

checklist.name: Suite green after the fix
checklist.description: `pytest` passes with all four cases executing (three original plus the new rejection case). A remaining failure, an error, or a skipped async test scores zero.

checklist.name: No real infrastructure and no new packages
checklist.description: MUST NOT introduce a real broker, a network call, or a new dependency in `requirements-dev.txt`. The doubles stay in-process.
